text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski Sunday opened a long distance power line between Skopje and Bitola.

- Ethnic Albanian parties PDP and NDP demanded at their electoral meetings this weekend a new platform for inter- ethnic relations in Macedonia. This means a complete autonomy of the Albanians, the Albanian nation's constituent position in the country and introduction of Albanian as a second language.

- Macedonia and Croatia to sign a free trade zone agreement soon. Macedonia has already concluded such an agreement with Slovenia and plans to propose the same model of agreement to Albania and Bulgaria.

- "Macedonia seeks new and institutionally regulated relations with the EU," the Macedonian premier Branko Crvenkovski said at the meeting of the Central European Initiative (CEI) in Graz. Macedonia expects to sign an agreement with the EU in January next year.
- Macedonian Moslems complain that the government has neglected their rights.
